claim: Tiny diffraction cameras replace most lenses
originalWording: Tiny diffraction cameras replace most lenses

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)
sources.locator: P02 2019 computing, quantum-based diffraction imaging paragraph

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: The specified pinhead-scale lensless/diffraction technology replaces most conventional camera lenses.
strict.rationale: Ordinary smartphone cameras still relied on lenses in 2019; tiny camera sensors did not fulfill the optical substitution. Computational imaging is widespread, but not equivalent to majority replacement of optics with the specified diffraction architecture.

evidence.title: Apple: iPhone X and Face ID
evidence.note: Announced September, retail availability November 3, 2017. Documented secure everyday owner recognition; not first-ever face recognition.

evidence.title: Canon: 2026 digital imaging system and market release
evidence.note: Current mainstream digital imaging and interchangeable optical lenses. Supports the present digital-camera ecosystem and persistence of lenses, not an exact historic film crossover year.

broader.criterion: Lensless diffraction or computational flat-optics replace conventional optical lenses in a substantial share of cameras.
broader.rationale: Smartphone cameras miniaturized photography using tiny multi-element glass/plastic lenses paired with computational processing, not by replacing lenses with pinhead-scale diffraction optics. Mainstream phone and standalone cameras still rely on optical lenses in 2026.
